source: Ministry of Agriculture training module "ជំនិតកម្មដំណាំខ្នុរសំរាប់កសិកម្ម" (Jackfruit Cultivation Techniques for Agriculture), prepared with participation from the Santisena organization, an elderly people's association, a charitable organization, and the CRS (Catholic Relief Services) agriculture program; content compiled with reference to fruit-tree materials and Prek Leap National School of Agriculture (សាលាជាតិកសិកម្មព្រែកលៀប).
text:
The module describes several pest and disease control methods, though part of this page's text was faint/garbled in the scan and could not be read with full confidence, so it is summarized here at a general level rather than translated word-for-word. Farmers are advised to apply a lime-based coating mixture around the base of the trunk as a protective measure. A chemical pesticide (identified by name as malathion) is used when insects are damaging the flowers; the text notes that whenever pesticide is used, a warning sign must be placed nearby because it is dangerous to people. Branches affected by disease should be cut off and then either buried or burned. There is also a reference to wrapping or binding affected areas to help repel harmful insects, but the exact method described for this step was not legible enough to translate reliably.

No diagram accompanies this section in the source; the page is text-only aside from a library accession stamp.
